RUNNER_TOKEN.description: Registration token from the GitHub UI. Go to Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner and copy the token from the ./config.sh command.

REPO_URL.description: Full GitHub repository URL (e.g. https://github.com/your-org/your-repo). Required for repo runners, leave empty for org runners.

ORG_NAME.description: GitHub organization name (e.g. your-org). Required for org runners, leave empty for repo runners.

RUNNER_SCOPE.description: Scope of the runner: repo (single repository), org (entire organization), or ent (GitHub Enterprise). Defaults to repo.

LABELS.description: Comma-separated labels for this runner. Reference these in workflow YAML with runs-on to target this specific runner.

RUNNER_NAME_PREFIX.description: Prefix for the auto-generated runner name. A random suffix is appended to ensure uniqueness across multiple instances.

CONFIGURED_ACTIONS_RUNNER_FILES_DIR.description: Directory where runner registration state is persisted across restarts.

RUNNER_WORKDIR.description: Working directory for workflow job execution inside the container.

DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE.description: Prevents the runner binary from self-updating, keeping the pinned image version in use.

UNSET_CONFIG_VARS.description: Clears GitHub credential environment variables after runner registration to prevent them from leaking into workflow steps.

START_DOCKER_SERVICE.description: Start a Docker daemon inside the runner VM, enabling container-based workflow steps and Docker actions. Safe to enable — each runner runs in its own isolated Linux VM.

token-instructions.content: Before starting, you need a **RUNNER_TOKEN** plus either **REPO_URL** (for repo runners) or **ORG_NAME** (for org runners).

setup-guide.content: Go to **Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner** on your repository or organization and copy the token from the `./config.sh` command. This token expires after 1 hour but the runner stays registered.
